title: Session format v1-to-v2 breaking change is unrecorded in CHANGELOG [Unreleased]
claim: The session JSONL on-disk format breaking change introduced at this head - FORMAT_VERSION 1 to 2, a required/ignorable_observation entry envelope, a runtime_input_binding header field, and v1 files becoming read-only so resume and fork refuse them - has no entry under CHANGELOG.md ## [Unreleased], so a 0.8.0 release would ship a silent durable-format break contrary to the repository's 0.x breaking-change recording policy.

evidence.detail: FORMAT_VERSION = 2 and LEGACY_FORMAT_VERSION = 1; new writers require a v2 header with a runtime-input binding (SessionWriter::create rejects other headers).
read_validated_with_recovery errors on v1 with 'legacy session is read-only because it has no runtime-input binding'; SessionWriter::open likewise refuses v1 (session.rs:464).
resume_session routes through read_validated_with_recovery, and fork_session calls resume_session, so both operations fail for v1 sessions; only list/show read paths still accept v1.

Full section read at audit_head: no session-format entry exists (grep for session/format/v2/envelope finds no format-change record); the Changed bullet 'sessions are never rewritten by load, normalization, resume, or fork' does not disclose that v1 sessions can no longer be resumed or forked at all.
Released builds shipped session persistence with resume, fork, export, and branching (0.7.x entries, e.g. lines 373-388), so v1 session files are real existing user data.

criterion_source: AGENTS.md 'Changelog and release': while on-disk formats remain 0.x, breaking changes are allowed only when deliberately scoped and recorded under ## [Unreleased].

title: opi-agent README (EN and ZH) still documents the superseded v1 additive session contract
claim: crates/opi-agent/README.md and README.zh.md describe the session format as header version = 1 with additive entries and skip-and-count recovery for unknown future entry types, while the build at this head writes version 2 with a required/ignorable envelope where an unknown required entry fails closed - the READMEs misdocument the durable-format compatibility and fail-closed boundary of a published crate in both language counterparts.

evidence.detail: 'Session storage is append-only JSONL: First line: SessionHeader (version = 1) ... Additive typed entries on the v1 header ... unknown future entry types (well-formed JSON with an unrecognized type, skipped and counted)'.
Same superseded contract in Chinese ('第一行：SessionHeader（version = 1）... v1 头部上的增补类型条目 ...'), plus a stale v1 reference in the overview paragraph.

Current format: version 2; every entry wrapped in an envelope declaring required or ignorable_observation; an unknown required entry returns InvalidData ('unknown required session entry type', session.rs:681); only an explicitly ignorable unknown observation is skipped and counted.

criterion_source: AGENTS.md 'Sources of truth': crate READMEs own current product and protocol facts; documentation must stay in lockstep with current behavior in both language counterparts.
reproduction: grep -n 'unknown required session entry type' crates/opi-agent/src/session.rs

title: Legacy-fixture acceptance tests write v2 sessions, leaving the v1 compat break untested at the product seam
claim: The registered byte-for-byte legacy-fixture verification for P17-MIG-001/MIG-002/P17-A13 no longer exercises the legacy v1 format: write_legacy_session builds fixtures with SessionHeader::new + SessionWriter::create, which at this head always produce v2 headers with runtime-input bindings, so all 'legacy session' acceptance tests run against v2 files and no product-level test pins the v1 resume/fork refusal behavior or its diagnostics.

evidence.detail: write_legacy_session uses SessionHeader::new(...) and SessionWriter::create(...); at this head SessionHeader::new derives a binding and writes version 2, and SessionWriter::create rejects non-v2 headers - the fixture is a v2 file with a bare model_change entry, not a v1 file.
SessionHeader::new calls new_with_runtime_input_binding with a derived default binding; FORMAT_VERSION is 2.

No coding-agent test asserts that resuming or forking a genuine v1 session fails with the typed read-only error; the refusal path (session_cli.rs:182, session_coordinator.rs resume) is unpinned at the seam users hit.
Genuine v1 files are hand-written only at the core reader layer (read/recovery semantics); the product resume/fork path for v1 is covered nowhere.

criterion_source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-phase17-deep-agent-core-semantic-closure-design.md P17-MIG-001 mechanical verification: 'Byte-for-byte legacy fixture tests.'
